hook_text: Maize meal gets expensive... and RICE sales take off. Markets whisper to each other. Listen.
clip_script: A poor harvest shoves maize meal up to twenty-five rand. In the rice aisle something odd happens: rice's own price has not moved, yet more shoppers reach for rice this week than last. Picture rice's demand curve — price up the side, quantity along the bottom, sloping down. It does not slide along itself; the entire curve steps to the right, because at every rice price there are now more willing buyers. Rival's price up, my demand up — the substitute signature. Partners pull the other way: if bread turns pricey, fewer sandwiches get made, and polony's whole demand curve steps to the left.
visual_style: A split-screen supermarket aisle: the maize meal tag climbing while trolleys stream to the rice shelf, a demand curve stepping right in glowing overlay.
pacing: Slow-build mystery — the unmoved rice tag — snapping into the rule as the curve visibly steps sideways.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to trace how every market pulls on its neighbours.
